catalog_quote: Le comorien est une langue purement accentuelle. Au niveau lexical, les syllabes se divisent en marquées et non-marquées. Il n'y a normalement pas plus d'une syllabe marquée par morphème, exception faite de certains thèmes nominaux (vraisemblablement) empruntés ou d'anciens mots composés, parfois difficilement décelables ... 3.8.1. Une particularité du comorien est que les pieds ne se forment qu'au niveau post-lexical, dans le cadre, donc, des groupes prosodiques de strate 1. L'algorithme de construction des pieds, en ndzuani, est le suivant : - la syllabe finale est extra-métrique (sauf si elle est marquée) - construire des pieds illimités et dominants à gauche - chaque pied est affecté d'un H sur sa syllabe finale - les H sont tous effacés à l'exception du premier du groupe. world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Ndzwani Comorian is not in the catalog. Both title hits are on-target but unreachable: Chamanga 1986/87 (Afrique et Langage 25; Glottolog pp. 55-63 vs Lafon pp. 35-54) is the one Shindzuani-specific accent study and exists only in print; Philippson 2005 (Tervuren volume, pp. 199-220) has no open copy (RMCA open-access list/repository, HAL, OpenAlex, Crossref, IA all empty) and is known here only through Patin's quotations on Shimaore. The best statement actually read is second-hand: Lafon 1991 (HAL, held by the project, copied to the ndzw1235 folder) summarises Ahmed-Chamanga 1987 and Philippson 1988 for anjouanais — accent penultimate by default, attracted by lexically 'marked' morphemes, retracting before a second marked syllable. Heepe 1920: 27 (held by the project) only presupposes an unstressed final syllable after the accent. Philippson's 1993 Persée review of Chamanga's Shindzuani lexicon was reachable for page 1 only (no accent content). Acquisition priority: Philippson 2005 and Chamanga 1986 (high); also Philippson 1988 Etudes Océan Indien 9 (not an item, named by Lafon as the source of the anjouanais rules).

new_statements.quote: Le comorien est une langue purement accentuelle. Au niveau lexical, les syllabes se divisent en marquées et non-marquées. Il n'y a normalement pas plus d'une syllabe marquée par morphème [...] L'algorithme de construction des pieds, en ndzuani, est le suivant : - la syllabe finale est extra-métrique (sauf si elle est marquée) - construire des pieds illimités et dominants à gauche - chaque pied est affecté d'un H sur sa syllabe finale - les H sont tous effacés à l'exception du premier du groupe. [p. 354:] lorsqu'un mot ne comporte aucune syllabe accentuée, un pied par défaut est construit sur sa syllabe pénultième, lorsqu'il apparaît en isolation.
new_statements.translation: Comorian is a purely accentual language. At the lexical level, syllables divide into marked and unmarked. There is normally no more than one marked syllable per morpheme [...] The foot-construction algorithm in Ndzuani is as follows: the final syllable is extrametrical (unless it is marked); build unbounded left-headed feet; each foot is assigned an H on its final syllable; all the H's are deleted except the first one of the group. [p. 354:] when a word contains no accented syllable, a default foot is built on its penultimate syllable when it appears in isolation.
new_statements.citation: Philippson, Gérard. 1991. Tons et accent dans les langues bantu d'Afrique orientale: étude comparative typologique et diachronique. Thèse de Doctorat d'Etat, Université Paris V René Descartes, 542 pp.

Au niveau lexical, les syllabes se divisent en marquées et non-marquées. Il n'y a' / p. 351 top: 'normalement pas plus d'une syllabe marquée par morphème, exception faite de certains thèmes nominaux..'; p. 351 §3.8.1: 'L'al…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent (realized as a high pitch) depends on lexically marked syllables: each morpheme may carry at most one marked syllable; the foot ends (and the H lands) on the marked syllable, and within a prosodic group only the first H survives. A word with no marked syllable takes default penultimate accent (the final syllable is extrametrical unless itself marked). In verbs the accent falls on the penult of the theme for unmarked radicals and on the object marker for marked ones (p. 276); accent may surface on the final, the penult, the theme-initial or any prefix depending on marking (pp. 276-277).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned; all H's but the first of the prosodic group are deleted.
new_statements.exceptions: Some (probably borrowed or old compound) nominal themes carry two marked syllables (p. 351 n. and fn. 1); a few phrasal examples contradict the group-formation rule (p. 353); the nominal-suffix -ni shows that some nominal themes are underlyingly accentless (ndzianí vs nyumbáni, p. 354).
new_statements.domain_note: Accent is computed post-lexically over the prosodic group (strate 1), not the isolated word; word-level default penult holds for words in isolation. Data are the author's own Ndzuani material (Philippson 1988 is the fuller treatment). System described as pitch accent-like: accented syllables high, others low.
new_statements.identity_note: Philippson 1991 describes 'le comorien (dialecte ndzuani)', i.e. the Anjouan variety = ndzw1235 itself (the author's own Ndzuani data); his remarks contrast it with ngazija (ngaz1238) and mwali (mwal1237). Lafon 1991 and Wikipedia speak of Comorian generally; Rombi 1983 is about Shimaore (maor1244).

new_statements.quote: pour Ahmed-Chamanga & Philippson en effet, chaque syllabe possède, comme propriété intrinsèque, d'être ou non "marquée"; dans les formes actualisées, la place de l'accent est déterminée par une combinatoire des syllabes marquées co-occurant dans une unité accentuelle (accent pénultien par défaut en cas d'absence totale de syllabe marquée) [...] la présence d'une autre syllabe marquée entraîne le recul de l'accent sur la syllabe précédant la deuxième marquée (règle des deux premières syllabes de Ahmed-Chamanga 1987:41, et règle n°1 de Philippson 1988:54)
new_statements.translation: for Ahmed-Chamanga & Philippson, each syllable has, as an intrinsic property, the feature of being 'marked' or not; in actual forms the place of the accent is determined by the combination of marked syllables co-occurring within an accentual unit (penultimate accent by default when no syllable at all is marked) [...] the presence of another marked syllable causes the accent to retract onto the syllable preceding the second marked one (Ahmed-Chamanga's 1987:41 'first-two-syllables rule', and Philippson's 1988:54 rule no. 1)
new_statements.citation: Lafon, Michel. 1991. Review article: Jouannet, Francis, 1989, Des tons à l'accent: essai sur l'accentuation du comorien. Swahili Language and Society: Notes and News 8: 45-64 (HAL halshs-00078493) — reporting Ahmed-Chamanga 1987 and Philippson 1988 on Shindzuani/anjouanais
new_statements.locator: printed p. 47, section 'I Sur l'accentuation' (the scanned text) and accompli discussion (the scanned text)
new_statements.reading: Shindzuani word accent is mobile and morphologically conditioned: penultimate by default, attracted to a lexically marked morpheme (e.g. perfective suffix: tsihúlu 'I bought'), and retracted to the syllable before the second marked syllable when two marked morphemes co-occur (nihúlu, tsióno). Rombi's scale (as cited by Lafon) calls the Shindzuani tone system 'assez dégradé'. Caveat: this is a specialist's review summarising the two primary studies, not a first-hand description; the primaries (Chamanga 1986/87, Philippson 1988, Philippson 2005) were not reachable. Heepe 1920: 27 independently presupposes an unstressed final syllable after the accent.
new_statements.found_by: works with stress in the title

sources.note: Comorian (Ndzuani data) is 'une langue purement accentuelle': syllables are lexically marked/unmarked (max one marked syllable per morpheme); feet are built post-lexically in the prosodic group with final syllable extrametrical, H on the last syllable of each foot, all H but the first deleted; a word with no marked syllable gets a default penultimate foot in isolation (p. 354); verbs: accent on the penult of the theme for unmarked radicals, on the object marker otherwise (p. 276).

Per Lafon 1991's review it is a metrical analysis of the Shindzuani verb: each morpheme is lexically 'marked' or not, accent falls on the penult by default when no syllable is marked, on a lone marked suffix (e.g. perfective -u: tsihúlu), and retracts to the syllable before the second marked syllable when two are present (nihúlu, tsióno). Only Shindzuani-specific accent study known.
